Research Center Energy Salix · Fast growing Energy Forest

From fast-growing willow to the building brick of the future

We grow selected energy willow on marginal land and along road and rail corridors, and turn it into renewable energy, long-term carbon storage and the Eco Bio Building Brick (EBBB).

One biomass platform

Four value pathways from the same willow

Selected Salix and Populus cultivars grow as short-rotation coppice on land that is not used for food, and on strips along roads and railways.

01

Eco Bio Building Brick

A construction material that locks carbon from willow biomass into the walls of buildings.

02

Carbon removal certificates

Roots, soil and biomass retain about 15 tonnes of CO₂ equivalent per hectare each year.

03

Bio-based materials

A renewable feedstock for bioplastics and other bio-based products.

04

Renewable heat and power

Locally grown biomass that replaces coal in heat and power generation.

The technology

From willow biomass to a building material

Willow biomass

Feedstock from road strips and marginal land, harvested every three years.

→
ECM

Ecocarbon mass

Interrupted pyrolysis keeps about 70% of the dry mass as carbon-rich material. Patent pending.

→

EBBB-I

Laboratory prototype developed with BEST GmbH, Austria.

Prototype expected by the end of November 2026. Performance testing and industrial validation are still ahead. Brick image is a concept rendering.
The overlooked land

Road and rail corridors become productive green strips

Neglected roadside belts are turned into rotational willow strips in three mechanised passes: clear the verge, till the strip, plant the cuttings. Lower establishment cost than conventional protective belts, fast growth and income from biomass.

12,000plants per kilometre, 6 rows
3 yearsbetween harvests
≈8 tdry matter per km per year

Status, October 2026

Where we are and what comes next

Today · TRL 3

  • 11 Salix cultivars registered in Ukraine, 2 in EU registration
  • Field sites in Ukraine: 9 sites, 9.5 ha
  • Research plots on marginal land in Germany and Poland
  • Collaboration in Ukraine, Portugal, Germany, Poland, Austria and the Netherlands

Next 12-24 months

  • November 2026: EBBB-I laboratory prototype with BEST GmbH
  • Tests: strength, thermal and moisture behaviour, fire, durability
  • Life-cycle assessment and carbon accounting for EBBB
  • First roadside demonstration corridor, 250 m module
  • First demonstration house built with EBBB
